title: Bermuda annual GDP
notes: Dates mark the end of each calendar year or quarter. Each row contains one observation. Missing observations are omitted, never replaced with zero.
Percentage values use the percent scale: 5 means 5%. Published growth is distinct from growth calculated from selected annual levels.
Values are snapshots of the supplied workbook’s cached results. Original workbooks retain formulas, revision history and full source references. Source workbook compilation date: 5 November 2026.
Real GDP uses 2013 prices. The 1996–2020 history retains an unknown publication vintage; 2021–2025 comes from the latest annual report. 2025 is provisional.

Calculated growth compares selected annual levels; published growth uses each report’s comparison and can differ. The supplied 2007 real GDP figure differs from the rebasing note by BD$0.072 million and is retained.
Annual industry GDP and quarterly expenditure GDP are different measures; annual values need not equal the sum of quarters.

Measure: Calendar-year GDP by industry at purchasers’ prices. Real GDP uses the 2013 benchmark. This is the official annual industry measure and is distinct from quarterly GDP by expenditure. Annual totals need not equal sums of the quarterly series.

Historical coverage: The 1996–2020 working history retains the supplied workbook values. Its publication date is unknown. These rows are labelled Supplied historical and have not been asserted to be the latest independently verified publication vintage.

Latest release: 2021–2025 levels and published growth come from the 2025 annual report, printed September 2026 and announced on 23 October 2026. The latest year is provisional; 2021–2024 are marked revised in the source.

Price-base evidence: The official rebasing note says the new 2013-benchmark series was extrapolated back to 1996. Supplied nominal and real GDP are equal in 2013. Comparisons for 2006–2013 largely agree with the official rebased series. Earlier 1996–2005 levels were not independently re-extracted from an official table.

Historical difference: Supplied real GDP for 2007 is BD$7,877.972 million; the rebasing note reports BD$7,877.9 million. The BD$0.072 million difference exceeds that table’s rounding interval. The supplied value is retained and the unknown historical vintage is flagged in the validation archive.

Overlap verification: All 10 supplied nominal and real GDP totals for 2020–2024 agree with the official 2024 report within its BD$1,000 reporting precision. This supports the supplied series’ interpretation but does not establish its publication date.

Growth columns: Calculated YoY growth equals the change between consecutive selected annual levels. Published growth is transcribed from the 2025 report for 2021–2025. Published and calculated rates can differ because of rounding and release-vintage differences, particularly at the 2020–2021 source transition.

Deflator and per capita: The implicit GDP deflator is calculated as nominal GDP / real GDP × 100, with 2013 = 100. Nominal GDP per capita is published BD$ per person for 2021–2025. No earlier per-capita series has been inferred.

Units and precision: GDP source tables use BD$ thousands, converted to BD$ millions by dividing by 1,000. Supplied workbook totals are in BD$, converted by dividing by 1,000,000. Displayed GDP levels have three decimal places; original supplied precision is retained in the stored values and CSV.

Revision audit: The source sheet retains the original 2021–2024 values alongside their replacements. The archive contains eight nominal/real revision comparisons. Raw PDFs, the supplied workbook, extraction text and validation results are preserved separately.

Missing and zero: Blank published growth or per-capita cells mean unavailable in the retained source inputs. They are not zero. The first calculated growth observation is blank because 1995 is outside the supplied series.

Validation: Checked latest report headers, GDP at basic prices plus net product taxes versus purchasers’ prices, 2024 overlap rounding, historical base comparisons, unique annual keys and saved workbook/CSV agreement. One small historical comparison difference is documented above.
description: GDP by industry at purchasers’ prices. Nominal and real GDP, growth, the GDP deflator and GDP per capita.
